title: Deterministic kernel bootstrap and soft-rollback path for mixed-ABI GPU fleets
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a deterministic, observable kernel bootstrap sequence and a non-destructive (soft) rollback mechanism for GPU shared-object upgrades to reduce flakiness during mixed-ABI rollouts. Current probe & symbol resolution playbook sometimes leads to nondeterministic ordering of symbol bindings across containers and causes subtle hangs or incorrect kernel selection on heterogenous fleets. This ticket implements a bootstrapping protocol and a relocation/alias table that allows new kernel bundles to be preferentially bound while preserving a quick, in-process soft-rollback path if runtime invariants are violated.

Background and motivation:
- Upgrades to CUTLASS / Triton / CUDA stacks have repeatedly triggered hard failures in production due to symbol collisions and non-deterministic loader behavior on nodes with multiple vendor libraries.
- Existing mitigations (delayed probe, namespace envs) reduce incidence but do not guarantee deterministic startup ordering; incidents linger as racey CI failures and customer-facing latency spikes during rollouts.
- A soft-rollback mechanism that can be invoked locally during init offers a safer deployment model and reduces the blast radius of partial upgrades.

Goals and non-goals:
- Goals: deterministic kernel load order, per-runtime relocation alias table, soft in-memory rollback within same process, richer telemetry for probe path decisions, CI/bench gating for canaries.
- Non-goals: cross-machine stateful rollbacks or rolling back persistent artifacts in registry (those are handled by existing artifact pipelines).

Design outline (high level):
1) Deterministic bootstrap coordinator: introduce a deterministic bootstrap layer invoked early in runtime init. It enumerates candidate kernel bundles, sorts them by a stable key (bundle-id, semantic-version, verified-hash), and selects the first compatible bundle via a capability matrix.
2) Relocation/Alias table: at load time, build an in-process relocation table that maps public symbol names to resolved symbol addresses for the selected bundle. The table is annotated with bundle metadata and a rollforward token.
3) Soft-rollback path: if runtime sanity checks fail during warmup (smoke ops / sample GEMM), flip the relocation table atomically to a previously-known-good bundle mapping without forcing a process restart. The old mapping remains quarantined for analysis.
4) Signature & integrity validation: verify signed bundle manifests and checksums prior to binding. Failure modes must be safe-fail to previous bundle if available.
5) Observability hooks: emit bootstep spans and probe decisions to tracing (trace-id, selected-bundle, fallback-reason) and a compact bootstrap telemetry event to metrics for rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic bootstrap orders bundles identically across repeated inits on same node under identical env
Relocation table successfully redirects symbol lookups and can be atomically swapped at runtime
Soft-rollback observable in user logs and avoids process restart for 95% of simulated regressions
All bridge cases covered in unit tests and e2e canary harness; canary shows no increase in regressions vs baseline
Signed-bundle verification implemented and failing signatures trigger safe-fallback to previous bundle
New telemetry emitted and dashboards created for bootstrap success/failure and fallback counts

Implement relocation/alias table and atomic swap primitive
Add lightweight smoke-warmup checks for GEMM/attn hot paths
Integrate signed-bundle verification and checksum validation
Add telemetry spans and metrics; update tracing schema
Create unit/integration tests for deterministic ordering and rollback path
Run canary on dedicated internal fleet; monitor rollback/telemetry metrics
Add CI gating and flakiness tests; document rollback operator workflow
